messages.content: Our teacher wants us to give a two-minute talk on any topic next week. I have no idea what to pick.
Pick something you already know well and enjoy, so you won't need much research. A hobby, a place you love or a skill you learned can all work. What do you like doing on weekends?
I like flying kites with my uncle on the terrace.
That could make a lovely talk. You could explain how a kite is made, how you choose a windy day, and share one funny moment with your uncle. Three short parts fit nicely into two minutes.
What if I forget my lines in front of everyone?

Don't learn it word for word. Write the three parts on a small card, one line each, and glance at it when you need to. Practise aloud at home two or three times, and time yourself so you know it fits.
My grandfather is moving in with us next week, and I have to share my room with him for a while.
That is a big change, and it is fair to have mixed feelings about it. Sharing a room takes some adjusting for both of you. How do you feel about it so far?
I love him, but I'm worried I won't get any privacy. I also study late.
Both worries make sense. You could ask your parents about a small study corner elsewhere for late evenings, like the dining table. A curtain or a bookshelf can also divide the room a little.
Should I say something to him too?

Yes, kindly and early. Ask him what he needs, like when he sleeps and wakes, and tell him your study hours. When you both know each other's routine, small problems are easier to solve before they grow.
Priya and Neha both invited me to their birthday parties, and they're on the same evening.
That is a tricky spot, since you probably don't want to hurt either friend. Are the parties at the same time, or is one earlier than the other?
Priya's starts at five and Neha's at seven. They live about twenty minutes apart.

Then you may be able to attend both. You could spend about an hour and a half at Priya's, leave around half past six, and reach Neha's a little before seven. Tell both of them your plan in advance so nobody is surprised when you leave or arrive.
My mom said she can drop me.
Good, that makes it easy. Confirm the timings with your mom today, and keep both gifts ready and labelled so you don't mix them up on the way.
I want to pack a healthier tiffin for myself, but I hate boring food.
Healthy does not have to mean boring. Colour and crunch make a big difference. What do you usually take now?
Mostly bread and jam, or chips if I'm in a hurry.

You could swap one thing at a time. Try a vegetable sandwich with a little chutney, or a roll made from last night's roti and sabzi. Add a fruit you like, such as a banana or a few grapes, for something sweet.
The roll idea is good. My mornings are rushed though.
Then fill the roll at night and keep it in the fridge. In the morning, you only need to pack it. A ready box takes less than a minute, which is faster than buying chips.
My family is taking an overnight train to Chennai, and I've never slept on a train before.
It can be a fun experience. The gentle rocking helps many people fall asleep. Do you know if you have an upper, middle or lower berth?
I think I have the upper berth.

The upper berth is quite private, and nobody needs it during the day, so you can lie down whenever you like. Keep a small bag with water, a torch and a light shawl up there with you, since trains can get cold at night.
What about my shoes and the big suitcase?
Put the suitcase under the lower seat, and lock it to the chain there if you have a lock. Put your shoes under the seat too, toes pointing in, so nobody trips over them in the dark.
My manager asked me to lead the team meeting tomorrow because she is on leave.
That shows she trusts you. Leading one meeting is a good chance to practise. Do you know what needs to be covered?
She sent me a short list of four points.

Then the meeting already has a shape. Start by thanking everyone and saying how long it will take. Go through the four points in order, give each a few minutes, and note any decisions. End by reading out who will do what.
What if two people start arguing?
Stay calm and neutral. You can say, "Both points are useful. Let's note them and let our manager decide when she's back." That keeps the meeting moving without taking sides.
We're celebrating Onam at my friend's house this year, and I don't know much about it.
Onam is a harvest festival celebrated mainly in Kerala. Families make flower carpets called pookalam and share a big vegetarian feast called the sadya. Are you joining for the meal?
Yes, the sadya. Is there anything I should know?

The sadya is usually served on a banana leaf, and many people eat with their right hand. There will be many small dishes, so take a little of each at first. Watch your friend's family and follow their lead.
Should I take something along?
A small box of sweets or some flowers would be a kind gesture. The flowers might even end up in the pookalam if they are making one.
I want to start running in the mornings but I get tired after five minutes.
That is very normal at the start. Most new runners go too fast. Have you tried mixing running with walking?
No, I just run until I can't anymore.
Try this instead: run for one minute, then walk for two, and repeat it six or seven times. Run slowly enough that you could still talk. Over a few weeks, run a little longer and walk a little less.
How often should I go?
Three mornings a week is a good start, with a rest day in between. Rest days give your legs time to recover. Tiredness is normal, but if something actually hurts, stop and take a break.
There's a bird building a nest on our window ledge.
How lovely. Do you know what kind of bird it is?
I think it's a pigeon. My dad wants to remove it.
Pigeons often nest on ledges because they feel safe there. If the nest has no eggs yet, now is the easiest time to decide. Once there are eggs or chicks, moving the nest can harm them.
Can we keep it until the babies leave?
You could ask your dad about that. Pigeon chicks usually leave the nest about a month after hatching. Keeping that window shut and not touching the nest will help both your family and the birds.
My book club picked a really long novel and I'm only on chapter three.
Long novels can feel slow at first, especially while the characters are being introduced. When is the club meeting?
In two weeks. The book has forty chapters.
That means about three chapters a day. If you read for half an hour before bed, you can probably keep up. Some days you will read more, which gives you a cushion.
And if I still don't finish?
Go anyway. You can share what you thought of the part you read, and the discussion may even make you want to finish it. Nobody in a book club should feel left out for being behind.
I keep comparing myself to my older brother. He's good at everything.
That can be tiring, especially when others compare you too. Is there something people say that makes you feel this way?
Relatives always ask why my marks aren't like his.
That hurts, and it is not a fair comparison. You are different people, with different strengths and different years. Your brother's marks say nothing about your worth.
But I'm not really good at anything.

It may feel that way right now, but strengths are not only marks. Being kind, being funny or being good with your hands all count. Think about what friends come to you for. That is often a clue to what you are good at.
My cat has started scratching the new sofa.
Cats scratch to keep their claws healthy and to mark their space, so she is not being naughty. Does she have a scratching post?
No. Do we really need one?
Yes, it gives her a better place to scratch. Put it right next to the sofa, since that is the spot she has chosen. Rub a little catnip on it, or play with a string near it, so she notices it.
Should we cover the sofa till then?
That is a good idea. A thick blanket over the scratched corner makes it less fun for her. Once she uses the post regularly, you can slowly move it to where you want it.
I bought a sketchbook a month ago and haven't drawn a single thing.
A blank sketchbook can feel strangely scary. Many people worry about spoiling the first page. Does that sound familiar?
Yes! I want every page to look good.

Then try this: on the first page, draw something messy on purpose, like scribbles or a cup drawn with your eyes closed. Once the first page is "ruined," the rest feels free. The sketchbook is for practice, not for showing off.
What should I draw after that?
Draw small things around you, like your shoes, a key or a mug. Give each one five minutes. Simple objects teach shape and shading, and you can finish them in one sitting.
I'm moving into my first rented flat with two friends.
Congratulations, that is an exciting step. Living with friends is fun, but it helps to agree on a few things early. Have you talked about chores yet?
Not really. We just assumed it will work out.

It often works out better with a simple plan. Make a chart for cooking, washing up and cleaning the bathroom, and rotate it every week. Also agree on how you will split shared costs like groceries and electricity.
What if one of them doesn't do their part?
Bring it up early, calmly and in private. Talk about the task, not the person: "The dishes were left for two days. Can we sort it out?" Small issues are easier to fix than a pile of resentment.
It's so hot this week that I can't sleep at night.
Heat makes sleep very hard. Is your room facing the afternoon sun?
Yes, the west side. It stays warm till midnight.
Keep the curtains closed in the afternoon to block the sun, and open the windows after sunset when the air outside cools. A damp cloth hung near the window can also cool the air a little.
Anything else that helps?
A cool bath before bed, light cotton clothes and cotton sheets all help. Some families sleep on a mat on the floor in summer, since it is often cooler than the bed.
My school choir has a concert next month and I got a small solo.
Congratulations! A solo, even a small one, means the teacher trusts your voice. How do you feel about it?
Excited but scared. My voice shakes when I'm nervous.

That is common, even for experienced singers. Slow breathing helps. Before your part, breathe in for four counts and out for six. Practising the solo many times also helps, because your body learns it and needs less effort on the day.
Should I practise in front of people first?
Yes, start small. Sing it for your family, then for a friend or two. Each small audience makes the real one feel less strange.
My grandmother just got her first smartphone and keeps calling me for help.
It's sweet that she turns to you. Learning a new phone at any age takes patience. What does she find hardest?
Mostly video calls. She can never find the button.
You could make her a simple guide on paper. Write three steps in big letters, maybe with small drawings of each button. Keep it next to her phone.
She also says the text is too small.
Most phones let you make the text and icons bigger in the settings. Do it for her once, and show her the change. Bigger text often makes everything else feel easier too.
I got into two colleges and I have to choose by Friday.
Congratulations on getting into both. That is a good problem to have. What are the main differences between them?
One is in my city and cheaper. The other is far away but has a better course.
Those are both real reasons. Try listing what matters most to you: the course, the cost, being near family, or living on your own. Rank them, then see which college fits your top two.
The course matters most, but I'm scared of living alone.

Many first-year students feel that fear, and for most it fades within a few months. You could ask the far college about hostels and student groups. Talking to a current student there may also make it feel less unknown.
I need new shoes for school but I can't decide between two pairs.
What are the two pairs like?
One looks really cool but pinches a little. The other is plain but comfortable.
Shoes that pinch in the shop usually feel worse after a full day of walking. Since you will wear them to school every day, comfort matters a lot.
But the cool ones are what everyone is wearing.
That is understandable. You could take the comfortable pair for school and save up for the stylish ones later for outings. Your feet will thank you on long school days.
Our colony is planning a cleanliness drive this Sunday and I want to help.
That is a kind thing to do. What kind of help do they need?
They asked for volunteers to collect plastic from the park.
Then wear clothes you don't mind getting dirty, closed shoes and gloves. Carry a water bottle and a cap if it is sunny. Keep separate bags for plastic and other waste so it can be sorted easily.
Can I bring my younger cousin? She's eight.
Yes, children often enjoy it. Give her a simple job, like holding the bag or picking up wrappers on the grass. Keep her away from glass or sharp things, and make sure she wears gloves too.
Our science project partner hasn't done any of his part, and the project is due Monday.
That is stressful, especially so close to the deadline. Have you talked to him about it yet?
I messaged him twice. He just says "I'll do it."
Try making it specific. Instead of asking in general, say, "Can you send me the chart by Saturday noon?" A clear task and a clear time are harder to ignore.
And if he still doesn't send it?
Then tell your teacher before Monday, calmly and honestly. Show what you have done. Teachers usually prefer hearing early to finding out on the deadline.
My parents are celebrating their twenty-fifth anniversary next month.
That's a wonderful milestone. Are you planning something for them?
Yes, with my sister. We want it to be a surprise.
A surprise can be lovely. You could collect old photos from relatives and make a small album, or invite close family for dinner. What do your parents enjoy most?
They love old songs and going to the beach.

Then you could combine both. Plan an evening walk on the beach, followed by dinner at home with their favourite songs playing. Ask each relative to write one short memory of them, and read a few aloud.
A new girl joined our class and she sits alone at lunch.
It is kind that you noticed. Starting at a new school can be lonely. Do you know her name?
Her name is Ayesha. I don't really know what to say to her.
Something simple works well. You could say, "Hi Ayesha, do you want to sit with us?" or ask where she studied before. You don't need a perfect line, just a friendly one.
What if my friends don't like it?
Most people warm up quickly when someone new is friendly. Introduce her to them by name. If one of them is cold to her, that says more about them than about you or Ayesha.
I tried making chapatis for the first time and they came out hard.
First chapatis are often hard, so don't worry. How did you make the dough?
I just mixed flour and water until it held together.
The dough may have been too stiff. It should feel soft and smooth. Knead it for a few minutes, then cover it and let it rest for about twenty minutes before rolling.
My mom said I cooked them too long too.
That can dry them out. Cook each side on a hot tawa only until small brown spots appear. Then it is done. You can keep them soft by stacking them in a box lined with a cloth.
We're going to visit Jaipur for three days during the winter break.
Jaipur is a good choice for winter, as the days are pleasant. Have you made a plan yet?
Not really. My parents want forts, my sister wants shopping.
Then you could split each day. Visit a fort in the morning, when it is cooler and less crowded, and spend the evening in a market. That way everyone gets something they like.
Which fort should we see first?
Many visitors start with Amber Fort, since it is large and needs the most time. Go early in the morning. On the other days you can see the smaller sights in the city.
I've been working from home for a month and I feel like I never stop.
That is a common problem with working from home. Without a commute, work can spill into the whole day. Do you have a fixed start and finish time?
I start at nine, but I keep checking messages till late.
Try setting a clear end time, maybe half past six, and turn off work notifications after that. Closing your laptop and putting it away can also signal that the day is over.
My boss sometimes messages at night though.
You could ask your boss directly what is urgent and what can wait till morning. Most managers are fine with next-day replies for normal tasks. Once you know, you can relax more in the evenings.
This is my first Christmas away from home. I'm living in a hostel.
Holidays can feel lonely when you are far from family. Are any other students staying in the hostel over the break?
A few, mostly from other states.
You could invite them for a small get-together. Each person could bring a snack from their home region and share one tradition. It can turn a lonely day into a warm one.
I'd also like to call my family that morning.
That's a good idea. Fix a time with them in advance so everyone is there. Seeing their faces on a call, then spending the evening with new friends, can make the day feel full.
I want to learn swimming but I'm twenty and I feel embarrassed.
Lots of adults learn to swim, so you would not be the only one. Many pools have adult beginner classes. Have you looked for one near you?
There's a pool near my office. They have classes at seven in the morning.
Early classes are usually quieter, which may help you feel less shy. Instructors who teach adults are used to nervous beginners.
What should I take on the first day?
A swimsuit, a towel, a cap and goggles are the basics. Take a change of clothes and a small bag for wet things. Reach a few minutes early so you can ask the instructor any questions.
We're going camping near a lake this weekend. It's my first time.
How exciting! Camping by a lake can be very peaceful. Will you be staying in tents?
Yes, with my scout group.
Then pack light but warm. Nights near water can be colder than you expect. Take a torch, a water bottle, a jacket and a spare set of clothes in a plastic bag so they stay dry.
What if I see snakes?

Most snakes avoid people and move away if left alone. Keep your distance, never try to touch or catch one, and tell your scout leader. Wearing closed shoes and using a torch at night also helps you see where you step.
I'm writing a short story for a competition but I'm stuck halfway.
Getting stuck in the middle is very common. What happens in your story so far?
A boy finds an old key in his grandmother's house, but I don't know what it opens.
That is a strong start. Ask yourself what the boy wants most. The key could open something linked to that wish, like a box of letters from a parent or a room nobody talks about.
I like the box of letters idea.
Then you have a direction. The letters could show him something new about his family. Let him find one surprising detail, and build the ending around how that changes him.
I auditioned for the lead in our school play and got a tiny role instead.
That is disappointing, especially if you worked hard for it. How are you feeling about it?
Embarrassed. My friend got the lead and everyone keeps congratulating her.
It is hard to be happy for a friend while you are hurting, and both feelings can exist together. You don't have to pretend you are fine, but you can still congratulate her.
Is a small role even worth doing?

Yes. Small roles teach you how a show runs, and directors notice people who do them well. Use rehearsals to learn from the lead role too. Next time, you will go into the audition with more experience.
My parents finally agreed to get a fish tank.
That is exciting. Fish can be calming to watch. Have you decided what fish you want?
I want lots of colourful ones.
It helps to start with a few hardy fish, since some colourful types need special care. Ask at the shop which ones are good for beginners and which can live together.
When can I put them in?
Set up the tank with water, the filter and plants first, and let it run for a while before adding fish. The shop can tell you how long. Then add only a few fish at a time, so the water stays clean.
I've started learning to knit from my aunt, and my rows keep getting uneven.
Uneven rows are normal when you are learning. Your hands are still finding the right tension. Do the stitches get tighter or looser as you go?
Tighter. By the end of the row, the needle barely fits.
That usually means you are pulling the yarn too hard, often from nerves. Try to relax your grip and slide each stitch onto the thick part of the needle, not the tip.
Should I start again?
You don't need to. Keep this piece as a practice square and see how your rows improve. Comparing the first rows with the last ones later will show you how far you have come.
Our kitchen sink keeps getting blocked.
That is annoying. Blocks usually come from food bits or grease going down the drain. Do you have a strainer in the sink?
No, we just rinse plates straight into it.
A simple mesh strainer catches most food bits. Scrape plates into the bin before washing, and never pour leftover oil down the drain, since it hardens in the pipe.
What about the block that's there now?
Pouring hot water slowly down the drain can sometimes loosen grease. If the water still won't go down, it is better to call a plumber than to keep trying strong chemicals.
The forecast says a cyclone might reach our coast this week.
That sounds worrying. The most important thing is to follow local news and official warnings. Do you live close to the sea?
About two kilometres away. My parents seem quite relaxed about it.
It still helps to prepare early. Keep torches, spare batteries, drinking water and some dry food ready. Charge phones and power banks, and keep important papers in a waterproof bag.
What if they tell us to leave?
Then leave when officials say so, and don't wait. Find out where the nearest shelter is, and decide in advance where your family will meet if you get separated.
My neighbour plays the sitar every evening and I'd love to learn.
What a lucky thing to hear every day. Have you ever spoken to your neighbour about it?
Just a hello. I'm not sure if it's okay to ask.
Many musicians are happy when someone shows real interest. You could praise the playing and ask how your neighbour started. That opens the topic gently without asking for lessons straight away.
And if he offers to teach me?
Then ask about timings and whether he takes fees, so things are clear from the start. Be on time, and practise between lessons. Teachers enjoy students who show steady effort.
My laptop has become really slow lately.
That is frustrating. Do you know how full the storage is?
It says only a small amount of space is left.
A nearly full drive can slow a computer down. Start by deleting large files you don't need, like old videos and downloads. Move photos to an external drive if you want to keep them.
I also have lots of programs that start when I switch it on.
Those can slow down startup. Look in the settings for startup apps and turn off the ones you don't need right away. Restart the laptop afterwards to see if it helped.
My college has a fest next month and I want to join the organising team.
That is a great way to meet people and learn new skills. Do you know which team you want to be on?
Maybe decoration or hospitality. I'm not sure.
Think about what you enjoy. Decoration suits you if you like making things with your hands. Hospitality suits you if you like talking to people and solving small problems quickly.
I like talking to people more.
Then hospitality sounds like your fit. When you sign up, mention a time you looked after guests or handled a crowd, even at a family event. It shows you already have some experience.
I'm buying my first winter jacket on my own this weekend.
That's a nice step. Do you know how cold it gets where you live?
Not very cold, maybe ten degrees at night.
Then you don't need a heavy jacket. A light padded one or a fleece would be enough. Check that you can move your arms easily and that the zip runs smoothly.
Should I buy one size bigger?
A little room is good, so you can wear a sweater underneath. Try it on over a thick top in the shop. If the sleeves cover your hands, it is too big.
The old library in our area might close because hardly anyone visits.
That would be a loss for the neighbourhood. Do you use it yourself?
I used to, as a kid. I'd like to help keep it open.
You could start by asking the librarian what would help most. Some libraries run reading clubs, homework hours or story time for children, which bring people in.
I could run a story hour for little kids on Saturdays.
That is a lovely idea. Pick short picture books, keep each session to about forty-five minutes, and put up notices in the building and nearby shops. Even a few regular families can make a difference.
I'm moving up to class nine and everyone says it's much harder.
Class nine does bring more depth, but many students manage it well with steady habits. What worries you most?
Science. There's physics, chemistry and biology all together.
Treat them as three short subjects, not one big one. Spend a little time on each every week, rather than cramming one at a time. Keep a separate notebook or section for each.
My friends say tuition is a must.
Not always. Many students do well by paying attention in class and asking teachers when they get stuck. Try the first few weeks on your own, and decide later if you need extra help.
My little brother is scared of the dark and wakes me up every night.
That must be tiring for you. Fear of the dark is very common in young children. How old is he?
He's six. He comes to my bed at two in the morning.
You could suggest a small night light in his room. Reading a calm story with him at bedtime can also help him feel safe before he sleeps.
My parents said I should be patient.
Patience will help, but you can also tell them what you need, since you need sleep too. Maybe they can take turns comforting him at night. That way it is not all on you.
My friend Rohan borrowed my bicycle two weeks ago and hasn't returned it.
That is frustrating, especially if you need it. Has he said anything about it?
No. I don't want to sound rude by asking.
Asking for your own things back is not rude. You could say, "Hey Rohan, I need my bicycle this weekend. Can you bring it on Friday?" A clear day makes it simple.
What if it's damaged?
Then talk about it calmly when you see it. He may not even know it got damaged. Ask him to help fix it, since it happened while he had it.
My roommate and I want to cook more and order less.
That's a good plan, and cooking together can be fun. How often do you order food now?
Almost every night.
Then don't try to cook every day at once. Start with three nights a week. Pick easy meals like khichdi, egg curry or pasta, and shop for those three meals on the weekend.
We always run out of time on weeknights.
Do some prep on Sunday. Chop onions, wash vegetables and boil a few eggs, then store them in boxes in the fridge. On weeknights, dinner then takes twenty minutes instead of an hour.
I'm flying alone for the first time to visit my aunt in Pune.
That is a big step. Do you know your flight time?
Yes, it's at six in the morning. I'm seventeen, by the way.
Then plan to reach the airport about two hours early, so around four. Keep your ID and ticket in one easy pocket. Pack your bag the night before, and check the rules for liquids in hand luggage.
What if I get lost inside the airport?

Airports have lots of signs and staff. Look for the screens showing your flight number and gate. If you are unsure, ask at the airline counter or any staff member. Text your aunt once you board and again when you land.
I have my first performance review next week and I don't know what to expect.
It's normal to feel unsure the first time. A review is usually a talk about what went well, what can improve and your goals. Have you been given a form to fill in?
Yes, they asked me to list my achievements.
Then think back over the year and write down specific things you did, with results if possible. For example, "Finished the report two days early" is better than "Worked hard."
What if they criticise me?
Listen calmly and take notes. Ask for an example if a point is unclear, and ask how you can improve. Treating feedback as information, not as an attack, usually makes the meeting go better.
We're making our own Ganesh idol from clay this year.
That's a wonderful idea. A clay idol is also kinder to rivers and lakes. Have you worked with clay before?
Only in school, a long time ago.
Start with simple shapes. Make the body from one large ball, then add the head, ears and trunk as smaller pieces. Keep a bowl of water nearby to smooth the joins.
Can we paint it?
Yes, but natural colours like turmeric are a better choice if you plan to immerse it in water. Let the clay dry fully for a few days before painting.
Our football team keeps losing in the last ten minutes of matches.
That often means players are getting tired near the end. Do you train for stamina, or mostly skills?
Mostly skills. We play small matches in practice.
Add some running to training, like short sprints with rest in between. Matches need bursts of speed again and again, and sprints build that.
What else can we do during the match?
Use your substitutes wisely, and bring fresh legs on before players are completely tired. Keep talking on the field, especially near the end, so nobody drifts out of position.
I saw fireflies in my grandparents' village last night. I'd never seen them before.
That must have been magical. Fireflies are harder to see in cities because of the bright lights. Where did you see them?
In the bushes near the paddy fields. Why do they glow?
Fireflies make light inside their bodies through a chemical reaction. They use the flashes to signal to each other, a bit like a code.
Can I catch one in a jar to show my friends?
It is better to let them be. Fireflies can get stressed or die in a jar. You could take your friends to see them one evening, or describe what you saw. Some sights are best left where they are.
My little sister is five and she doesn't like books at all.
Many young children warm up to books slowly. What does she like doing most?
She loves animals and drawing.
Then try picture books about animals, with big colourful pictures and only a few words on each page. Let her choose the books herself at the library.
She gets bored when I read to her.

Try making it lively. Use funny voices for the animals and ask her what she thinks will happen next. After reading, she could draw her favourite part. That links the story to something she already loves.
Is it okay to ask the teacher the same doubt twice? I didn't understand it the first time.
Yes, it is completely okay. Teachers would rather explain again than have you stay confused. Asking twice shows you care about understanding.
But the other kids might laugh at me.

Some might, but many of them probably have the same doubt. If you feel shy in class, you can catch the teacher after the lesson or during a free period. You could say, "I tried, but I'm still stuck on this part."
Guess what, I'm going to be a big sister! Mom told us yesterday.
That's wonderful news! How do you feel about it?
Happy, but also a bit worried. What if they love the baby more?

That is a very common worry, and it's okay to feel it. A parent's love doesn't get divided when a new baby comes. It grows to cover everyone. Babies do need a lot of time, though, so things will feel busy for a while.
Can I help with the baby?
Yes, older siblings can be great helpers. You could fetch nappies, sing songs or show the baby colourful toys. Ask your parents which jobs are safe for you.
I want to pick the baby's name.

That's sweet. Naming is usually the parents' choice, but you could make a short list of names you like and share it with them. Even if they choose another name, they will love that you thought about it.
How do I say sorry to a friend after I said something mean in anger?

Say it soon, in person if you can, and keep it simple. Name what you said, say it was wrong, and don't add "but." For example: "I'm sorry I called your idea stupid. It wasn't fair, and I was angry about something else."
What if she's still upset after that?
Then give her some time. An apology doesn't have to fix everything at once. Be kind to her in the days after, and let your actions show that you meant it.
Mom's out tonight and I'm in charge of dinner for me and my little brother. I'm fourteen.
That's a nice chance to cook. What is there in the kitchen?
Eggs, bread, onions, tomatoes and some cheese.
You could make egg bhurji with onions and tomatoes, and toast the bread on the side. It's quick, filling, and most kids like it.
I've never made bhurji. Is it hard?

Not at all. Chop one onion and one tomato. Fry the onion in a little oil until soft, add the tomato and a pinch of salt, then crack in the eggs and stir until they are fully cooked. It takes about ten minutes.
My brother hates tomatoes.
Then cook his share first with just onion and eggs, and make yours with tomatoes afterwards. You could melt a little cheese on his toast to make up for it.
We're going to Goa next week and I can't swim well.
You can still have a great time in Goa. There's a lot to do beyond swimming. Are you staying near a beach?
Yes, right by the sea. My friends will want to go in the water.
You can enjoy the shallow water where it is only knee-deep, and stay close to the shore. Only go in where lifeguards are on duty, and follow their flags.
What do the flags mean?
On many beaches, red means the sea is dangerous and you should stay out, and yellow means take care. Rules can differ from beach to beach, so read the notice board or ask a lifeguard.
What else can we do apart from the beach?
You could visit old churches and forts, walk through a spice farm, or explore a local market. Evening walks along the beach at sunset are lovely too.
My friends want to rent scooters.
If you do, make sure the rider has a valid licence and everyone wears a helmet. Roads can be narrow and busy in the evenings, so ride slowly and avoid riding late at night.
I made a mistake in a report that went to a client. My stomach is in knots.

That feeling is awful, but mistakes like this happen to almost everyone at work. The best thing is to tell your manager quickly, explain what went wrong and suggest a fix. Owning it early usually counts for more than the mistake itself.
Should I contact the client myself?
Check with your manager first. Some companies want one person to talk to the client, and your manager may want to send the correction. Have a corrected version ready so the fix can go out fast.
Holi is next week. My mom says I can play only if I'm careful.
That sounds fair. Holi is a lot of fun, and a few simple steps keep it safe. Are you playing at home or with friends nearby?
In our building compound with my friends.
Then wear old clothes that cover your arms and legs. Rubbing a little oil on your skin and hair before playing makes the colour easier to wash off later.
Some kids use water balloons.
Water balloons can hurt if thrown hard, especially near the face. Ask friends to throw gently, aim below the shoulders, and throw only at people who are playing.
What about the colours?
Dry, natural colours are gentler than bright chemical ones. Keep colour away from eyes and mouth. If any gets in your eyes, wash them with clean water and tell an adult.
Our badminton club is having a doubles tournament and my partner is much better than me.
That can feel like pressure, but it is also a chance to learn. What part of your game worries you most?
My serve. I keep hitting it into the net.
Work on a short, gentle serve first. Keep your wrist steady and push the racket forward smoothly instead of swinging hard. Practise twenty serves a day until the tournament.
Should I tell my partner I'm nervous?
Yes, that usually helps. Good partners want to know so they can support you. You could also agree that they cover more of the court during long rallies.
Why do leaves change colour before they fall?

Leaves are green because of a substance called chlorophyll. When days get shorter and cooler, some trees stop making it. The green fades, and yellow and orange colours that were hidden underneath start to show.
Then where does the red come from?

Red is a bit different. In some trees, new red colours are made in the leaves during autumn, often when days are sunny and nights are cool. That is why some years have brighter red leaves than others.
Most English books feel too hard for me, but I really want to read more.
That is a common start, and it gets easier with the right books. What kind of stories do you enjoy in your own language?
Mysteries, mostly.

Then try short mystery books written for younger readers, or graded readers made for learners. The language is simpler, but the stories are still fun. Pick a book where you know most of the words on a page.
Should I look up every word I don't know?
No, that slows you down too much. Guess the meaning from the sentence and keep reading. Look up only words that keep coming back or that stop you from following the story.
How much should I read every day?
Even fifteen minutes a day helps, if you do it most days. A regular time, like after dinner, makes it easier to keep going. Over a few months, books will start to feel lighter.
I've been feeling lonely since my best friend moved abroad.
That's a real loss, and it makes sense to miss her. Distance changes a friendship, but it doesn't have to end it. Do you two still talk?
Sometimes, but the time difference makes it hard. And I don't have anyone else close here.

You could set one fixed time each week to call, when you're both free, so it doesn't depend on luck. Here, try joining one activity you enjoy, like a club or a class. New friendships often grow slowly from seeing the same faces every week.
Our dog Bruno is getting old. He's twelve and sleeps most of the day.
Older dogs often sleep more and slow down, much like older people. Twelve is a good age for many dogs. How is he eating and moving around?
He eats fine but finds stairs hard now.
You could keep his bed and water on the ground floor. A rug or mat on slippery floors gives him better grip. Short, gentle walks are often better for older dogs than long ones.
Should we take him to the vet?
Yes, regular check-ups are a good idea for older dogs. A vet can look at his joints and tell you what will keep him comfortable.
I'm scared of losing him.
That fear shows how much you love him. For now, enjoy the time you have together: gentle walks, his favourite treats, quiet time sitting with him. Those moments matter to him too.
I want to start a collection of something, but I don't know what.
Collections are fun because they grow over time. Do you want things you can display, or things that fit in a small box?
Something small. My room isn't big.
Then coins, stamps, postcards or bookmarks would work well. Coins from different years are easy to find in everyday change, and they fit in a small album.
Coins sound fun. How do I keep them organised?
Sort them by year or by place, whichever you find more interesting. Write a small label for each one with where and when you got it. That little story often becomes the best part of a collection.
What's the easiest way to keep my room tidy? It's always a mess by Friday.
Try a ten-minute tidy every evening instead of one big clean-up. Put clothes away, clear your desk and throw out rubbish. Small daily resets stop the mess from piling up.
My problem is clothes. They end up on my chair.

Many people have a "chair pile." Give yourself one hook or basket for clothes you will wear again, and put everything else in the wash or the cupboard straight away. A clear place for each thing makes tidying faster.
There's a thunderstorm coming, and my little sister is scared.
Storms can feel scary, especially to small children. How old is she?
She's four. She hides under the bed when it thunders.
You can help her feel safe by staying close and speaking calmly. Explain that thunder is just the loud sound that comes after lightning, and that you are both safe inside.
Is there a game we can play?
Yes, try counting. When you see lightning, count slowly until you hear the thunder. A longer count means the storm is farther away. It turns the storm into a game and gives her something to do.
Should we stay away from the windows?
Yes, that is sensible. Sit in an inner room, away from windows, and stay indoors until the storm passes. Your calm voice will help her more than anything else.
Can you learn to sing if you have a bad voice?

Yes, most people can improve a lot with practice. Singing is a skill, like riding a bicycle. Learning to listen carefully and control your breath makes a big difference, even for people who think they have a "bad" voice.
Where should I start?

Start by humming along to simple songs and matching the notes. Then sing slow songs in a comfortable range, not too high or low. A teacher or a choir can help you improve faster, but daily practice at home works too.
My dad wants me to teach him how to make a spreadsheet for the house budget.
That sounds like a useful project to do together. Has he used a computer much before?
A little. He can type and send emails.
That's a good start. Begin with the basics: rows go across, columns go down, and each box is a cell. Make a simple table with three columns: the item, the amount and the month.
How do we add up the totals?
Most spreadsheet programs have a sum formula. Select the cell below the amounts and type something like =SUM(B2:B10), which adds everything from B2 to B10. Show him once, then let him try it himself.
He keeps typing over the formulas by mistake.
That happens a lot. You could colour the formula cells light yellow, so he knows not to type there. Some programs also let you lock certain cells.
Thanks, he's actually enjoying it now.
That's lovely to hear. Learning together can be fun for both of you. Next, you could show him how to make a simple chart, so he can see where the money goes each month.
I'm in my first year of college and I can't keep up with the lecture notes.
That's common in first year, since lectures move faster than school classes. Try writing only key words and short phrases, not full sentences. Leave space so you can fill in details later.
And when do I fill them in?
Do it the same day, while you still remember the lecture. Spend fifteen minutes going through your notes and filling gaps from the textbook or a friend's notes. It also counts as revision.
My friend's birthday is on Saturday, and I have only two hundred rupees for a gift.
You can find something thoughtful for that amount. What does your friend like?
She loves reading and drinking tea.
Then you could get a nice bookmark and a small packet of tea. Add a card with a handwritten note about a favourite memory you share.
I like the bookmark idea. Should I make one instead of buying?
That could be even more special. Use thick card, decorate it with her name or a line she likes, and cover it with clear tape so it lasts. Handmade gifts show effort.
What should I spend the money on then?
Spend some on good card and markers, and the rest on a small packet of her favourite tea. Wrap them together with a ribbon. It will look like a little reading kit.
Some kids on our street are being mean to the new family's son.
That's not okay, and it's good that you care. How old is he, and what are the other kids doing?
He's about ten. They make fun of how he speaks.
You don't have to fight anyone to help. Walk with him, include him in a game, or talk to him in a friendly way when others are around. Having even one friend makes a big difference.
Should I tell an adult?
Yes, especially if it keeps happening or gets worse. You could tell your parents or his parents what you've seen. Adults can step in in ways that kids often can't.
I lost my school ID card and we need it to enter the building tomorrow.
That's stressful, but it's usually easy to sort out. When did you last see it?
I think in the bus this afternoon.
You could ask the bus driver or conductor tomorrow morning, in case someone found it. Also check your bag pockets, your blazer and your desk at home one more time.
I checked everywhere at home. It's not there.
Then go to school a little early tomorrow and tell the guard and the office. Most schools have a way to let students in without an ID for a day. Ask how to apply for a new card.
Will I get in trouble?
Probably not much, especially if you report it honestly. Losing things happens to everyone. You might have to pay a small fee for a new card.
Okay. I'll ask my mom to write a note too.
That's a good idea. A note from a parent makes it even easier for the office. Put it in your bag tonight so you don't forget it.
My parents argue a lot lately and it makes me feel scared.
I'm sorry. It's hard to hear people you love argue, and feeling scared is a normal reaction. Do you feel safe at home?
Yes, they don't hurt anyone. They just shout.
I'm glad you're safe. Arguments between adults are not your fault, even when they argue about things that involve you. It's not your job to fix it.
What can I do when it happens?

You could go to your room, put on music or read, or sit with a sibling. Later, when things are calm, you could tell one of your parents how the shouting makes you feel. A trusted relative or a school counsellor is also someone you can talk to.
Is it weird that my closest friends are online and I've never met them?
Not weird at all. Many people make real friendships through shared interests online. What matters is that the friendship is kind and respectful.
My parents worry about it.

That's understandable, since they can't see who these people are. You could tell them a bit about your friends and what you talk about. Keep personal details like your address and school private, and never agree to meet someone without a trusted adult knowing.
I want to bake a cake for my dad's birthday but we don't have an oven.
You can still bake a cake. Many people use a pressure cooker or a heavy pan on the stove. Have you seen it done before?
No. Is it hard?

It needs some care, but it's doable. People usually put a layer of salt in the cooker, place a stand on it and set the cake tin on top. Remove the gasket and the whistle, then cook on low heat. Ask an adult to help the first time.
How do I know when it's done?
Push a toothpick or knife into the centre. If it comes out clean, the cake is ready. If wet batter sticks to it, cover it again and check after five minutes.
Hey, I'm planning a solo trip to Rishikesh. Any tips for a first-timer?

Rishikesh is a lovely first solo trip, with the river, the hills and lots of walking. Book a stay near the main areas so you can walk to most places. Keep a copy of your ID, and share your plans with someone at home each day.
Is the river safe for a dip?

The Ganga flows fast there, even where it looks calm. If you want to dip your feet, stay at the ghats where other people are, hold on to the chains, and don't go deep. Avoid going in at all after dark.
I want to ask for a raise but I don't know how to bring it up.
It helps to plan it rather than mentioning it in passing. How long have you been in your role?
Almost two years. I've taken on a lot more work since I joined.
That's a strong point. Write down the new tasks you handle and any good results. Then ask your manager for a short meeting, so the conversation has its own time.
What do I actually say?
Keep it calm and factual. For example: "Over the last two years, my role has grown to include these tasks. I'd like to discuss whether my pay can reflect that." Then let your manager respond.
What if they say no?
Ask what you would need to do to be considered later, and when you can talk about it again. A clear answer and a date give you something to work towards.
What do people do during Eid?

Celebrations vary, but many families start the day with special prayers, then wear new clothes and visit relatives and friends. Sweet dishes like sheer khurma are common, and elders often give children small gifts of money called eidi.
My neighbour invited us over. What should I say when I arrive?
"Eid Mubarak" is the usual greeting, and it means "blessed Eid." Smile, say it to each family member you meet, and accept the food they offer. A small box of sweets is a kind thing to bring along.
I'm coaching my little cousin's cricket team for fun. They're all eight or nine.
That sounds fun. At that age, enjoying the game matters more than winning. How many kids are there?
Ten. They all just want to bat.
That's very common. Give everyone a fixed turn to bat, maybe six balls each, so nobody feels left out. Change the batting order every session.
How do I keep the fielders interested?
Make fielding a game. Give points for clean catches and quick throws, and cheer loudly for good stops. Kids pay attention when they feel their job counts.
One boy cries when he gets out.
Some children find losing hard. Speak to him privately and kindly, and tell him what he did well before he got out. Remind everyone that every player gets out sometimes.
Should I keep score in matches?
You can, but keep it light. At that age, celebrating good moments matters more than the final score. Give a small cheer for the best catch or the most improved player each week.
My grandmother says it'll rain soon because the ants are moving their eggs. Is that true?
There may be something to it. Some people have noticed ants moving to higher ground before rain, possibly because they sense changes in the air. It isn't a reliable forecast, though.
What other signs do people look for?
People often watch the sky. Dark, heavy clouds building up in the afternoon, a sudden cool breeze or the smell of wet earth can all mean rain is close.
Why does rain smell like that?
Part of that smell comes from oils and other substances in dry soil, which are released into the air when the first drops hit the ground. The smell even has a name: petrichor.
My teacher says I should keep a reading journal. What do I even write in it?
Keep it simple. After each reading session, write the date, the pages you read and two or three lines about what happened. Add one thing you liked or a question you have.
That sounds a bit boring.
You can make it more personal. Copy a sentence you loved, draw a scene, or write what you would do in the main character's place. The journal is for you, so it can look however you like.
Today was the worst day. I spilled juice on my shirt, missed the bus and forgot my homework.
That sounds like a really rough day, one thing after another. How are you feeling now?
Annoyed. And tired.
That makes sense. Days like that wear you out. It might help to do something small and comforting this evening, like a warm bath or a favourite snack.
I still have to explain the homework tomorrow.
Tell your teacher honestly that you forgot it, and offer to bring it the next day. Most teachers are understanding when it doesn't happen often. Put it in your bag tonight so tomorrow starts better.
Okay. Thanks for listening.
Anytime. Bad days end, and tomorrow is a fresh start. Get some good sleep tonight.
Can my dog have a little chocolate as a treat?
No, please don't. Chocolate is harmful to dogs, even in small amounts, and dark chocolate is the worst. Keep it somewhere your dog cannot reach.
What treats are safe then?
Dog treats from a pet shop are made for them. Some plain foods, like small pieces of boiled chicken or carrot, are often fine too. Check with a vet if you're unsure about a particular food.
My uncle gave me his old camera and I don't know where to start.
What a nice gift. Old cameras can still take beautiful pictures. Do you know if it's digital or film?
Digital. It has lots of buttons.
Start in the automatic mode, so the camera handles the settings. Think about what you point it at and how you frame the picture. Settings can come later.
What should I photograph first?
Try everyday things: your street, your family at home, plants on the balcony, or light coming through a window. Photograph the same object from three different angles and see which one you like.
My photos always look a bit dull.
Light makes a big difference. Try shooting in the early morning or late afternoon, when the light is softer and warmer. Indoors, stand near a window rather than using the flash.
Should I share them somewhere?
You could, if you like. Sharing with family or a local photography club is a good first step, and their comments can help you grow.
We're painting my bedroom this weekend. I get to choose the colour!
How exciting. What colours are you thinking about?
Bright orange or dark blue.
Both can look great. Bright orange feels lively and warm, while dark blue feels calm and cosy. Since it's a bedroom, think about how you want to feel when you go to sleep.
Calm, I guess. But dark blue might make the room look small.
You could paint just one wall dark blue and keep the others light. It adds colour without making the room feel smaller. Try a small patch first and look at it in daylight and at night.
Why does it feel colder on a windy day even if the temperature is the same?
Wind carries away the thin layer of warm air that sits next to your skin. Your body keeps losing heat to warm a new layer, so you feel colder. People call this wind chill.
So should I wear more layers on windy days?
Yes, and a windproof outer layer helps most. A jacket that blocks the wind keeps the warm air close to your body. Covering your ears and neck also makes a big difference.
I want to make a playlist for a long car ride with my family.
That's a fun job. How long is the ride, and who is going?
About six hours. My parents, my grandma and my cousin, who's twelve.
Then aim for a mix everyone enjoys. Ask each person to pick ten songs they love. Mixing old songs for your grandma with newer ones for your cousin keeps everyone happy.
What if people fight over the music?
Take turns. Play a few songs from each person in a row, so everyone knows their turn is coming. You could also keep one quiet hour after lunch, when people may want to nap.
Good idea. Grandma does sleep a lot in the car.
Then put some soft, slow songs in that hour. She can rest, and everyone else can still enjoy the music at a low volume.
Someone sent me a message saying I won a prize and asking for my bank details.
That sounds like a scam. Real prizes don't ask for bank details or passwords over a message. Don't click any links or reply with personal information.
Should I just delete it?
Yes, you can delete it and block the number. If it came on a family phone, tell a parent as well. Warning friends and family about messages like this helps them stay safe too.
My college roommate and I have very different sleep schedules.
That can be tough in a shared room. What are your schedules like?
I sleep at eleven. He stays up till three playing games.
That's a big difference. Has the noise or the light been keeping you awake?
Both. His screen lights up the whole room, and he talks to his teammates.
It may help to talk to him calmly at a time when you're both relaxed, not at midnight. Explain that you need sleep for morning classes, and ask if he can use headphones and talk quietly after eleven.
What if he says no?
Try to find a middle ground. He could play in a common room after a certain time, or turn the screen brightness down. An eye mask and earplugs can also help on your side.
And if nothing changes at all?
Then speak to your hostel warden or whoever is in charge of rooms. Explain what you've tried. They deal with these problems often and may be able to help or offer a room change.
How do I know if a second-hand bicycle is in good condition?
Check the brakes first: squeeze them and push the bike forward. It should stop firmly. Then spin both wheels to see that they run straight and don't wobble. Look at the chain for rust.
The seller wants me to decide right now.
It's fair to take a short test ride before deciding. If the seller won't let you ride it at all, that is a reason to be careful. A good deal will usually still be there after ten minutes.
Our society wants to plant trees along the road. I'm on the planning team.
That's a lovely project. Do you know how many trees you're planting?
Around twenty. We're not sure which ones to choose.
Native trees that suit your local climate are usually best, since they grow well and support local birds. A nearby nursery can suggest good ones for your area.
Who will water them?
You could make a simple rota, where each family looks after one or two trees. Give each tree a small name tag. People take more care when a tree feels like "theirs."
Should we involve the children too?
Yes, they usually love it. Let children help plant, paint the tree guards or water the trees in the evening. Watching a tree they planted grow can make them care about it for years.
Can you help me plan my exam timetable? I have six exams in two weeks.
Yes, let's keep it simple. Which exams come first, and which subjects feel hardest?
Maths is first and hardest. English is last and easiest.

Then start with maths today and give it the most time early on. Study two subjects each day, one hard and one easier, so you don't get tired. Keep the last day before each exam just for revising that subject.
Where should I fit in breaks?
Take a short break every forty-five minutes or so, and a longer one after lunch. Keep one evening each week free to rest. A plan with breaks is easier to stick to than one without.
My grandmother keeps telling the same stories again and again.
That can feel repetitive, but those stories often matter a lot to her. People tend to return to memories that are important to them. Listening patiently can mean a great deal to her.
Is there a way to make it more interesting for me?

You could ask questions she hasn't answered before, like "What did you wear that day?" or "What happened next?" You might hear new details. You could also record her telling them, so the family keeps them for years.
Me and my friends want to start a band but we keep fighting about the name.
Band names cause more fights than you'd think. How many of you are there?
Four. Everyone has a favourite and nobody wants to give up.
Try this: each person writes three names on slips of paper. Put them all in a bowl, read them out, and cross out any that two or more people dislike. Then vote on what's left.
What if it's still a tie?
Pick one name for now and agree to try it for a month. If it doesn't feel right after a few practices, you can change it. Lots of bands change their names early on.
That takes the pressure off.
Exactly. The music matters more than the name, especially at the start. Spend your energy on practice, and the right name may even turn up along the way.
What's a simple snack I can make without a stove?
You could make bhel with puffed rice, chopped onion and tomato, a squeeze of lemon, salt and some sev. Or slice a cucumber and an apple and sprinkle them with a little chaat masala.
The bhel sounds good. Can I make it ahead of time?
Mix the dry and wet parts only just before eating, or the puffed rice will go soggy. You can chop the vegetables earlier and keep them in a box in the fridge.
My passport expires in five months, and we're travelling abroad in two.
It's good that you noticed early. Many countries want your passport to stay valid for some months after you arrive, often six. Have you checked the rules for the country you're visiting?
No. How do I find out?
Check the official website of that country's embassy. Your airline or travel agent can also tell you. Do it soon, because renewing a passport can take time.
If I need to renew it, what do I need?
Usually your current passport, proof of address and the application form. The exact list can change, so check the official passport website before you book an appointment.
I'll do it this week.
That's a wise plan. Keep photocopies of your old and new passports somewhere safe, too.
My coworker keeps interrupting me in meetings.
That's frustrating, especially when you have something to say. Does it happen every time, or only on some topics?
Almost every time I speak.
You could calmly say, "I'd like to finish my point, and then I'd love to hear yours." Keep your tone friendly. Often, naming it once is enough.
And if it continues?
Then speak to your coworker privately. They may not realise they're doing it. If nothing changes after that, you could mention it to your manager and ask for support.
We're hosting a Pongal lunch for friends who've never had it.
That sounds lovely. Pongal is a harvest festival from Tamil Nadu, and the dish of the same name is made from rice and moong dal. You could serve both sweet pongal with jaggery and savoury ven pongal.
What else should go on the menu?
Simple sides go well, like coconut chutney, sambar and a vegetable dish. Serve it on banana leaves if you can, which makes it feel special. Explain each dish as your friends try it.
Our school sports day is next week and I signed up for the long jump.
That's exciting! Long jump is all about speed and timing. Have you tried it before?
Only once. I keep stepping over the board.

Measure your run-up. Stand at the board and run away from it at your normal speed, counting your steps. Mark where you are after about twelve steps. Starting from that mark helps you reach the board on the right step.
Why is the sea salty but river water isn't?

Rivers carry small amounts of salt and minerals from rocks into the sea. When sea water evaporates, the water rises into the air, but the salt stays behind. Over a very long time, the salt has built up in the sea.
So rivers have salt too?
Yes, but only a tiny amount, so we can't taste it. River water keeps flowing and is refilled by rain, so the salt never builds up the way it does in the sea.
Is the Dead Sea salty for the same reason?
Yes, in a similar way. Water flows into the Dead Sea, but no river flows out of it. The water evaporates in the heat and the salt stays, so it is much saltier than the ocean.
Can people float in it?
Yes, easily. The salt makes the water very dense, so people float on the surface. Visitors often lie back in the water as if they were on a bed.
I lent my favourite book to my cousin and it came back with a torn cover.
That is upsetting, especially with a favourite book. Did your cousin say anything about it?
She said sorry, but she didn't offer to fix it.
It may help to tell her how you feel, calmly: "That book means a lot to me. Could you help me fix the cover?" Clear tape or a new paper cover can save it.
I don't want to lend her books anymore.

That's your choice, and it's okay to be careful with special books. You could lend her ones you don't mind as much, or read together at your place. That way you can still share stories without the worry.
Do you think it's better to study with music or in silence?

It depends on the person and the task. Many people find silence better for reading and memorising, while soft music without words can help with simple tasks like copying notes. Have you noticed which works for you?
I usually play songs, but I end up singing along.
That's a sign the songs are pulling your attention away. Try music without lyrics, or switch it off for the hardest subjects and keep it for easier ones.
Silence feels too quiet at home, though.
Then try gentle background sound, like a fan, rain sounds or quiet instrumental music at low volume. The aim is a steady sound you soon stop noticing.
I'll try rain sounds tonight for history.
Good plan. After the session, notice how much you remember. Comparing a few nights will tell you what suits you best.
Mom is turning fifty and keeps saying she wants "no fuss." Should we still do something?

You can respect "no fuss" and still make the day feel special. A quiet breakfast she doesn't have to cook, a handwritten card from each family member, or her favourite meal for dinner are all low-key ways to celebrate.
Can we invite her sisters?

That might be lovely, but check what "no fuss" means to her first. You could ask her lightly if she'd like to see her sisters that week. If she seems happy, invite them for a small tea instead of a big party.
My two closest friends had a big fight and both want me on their side.
That's an uncomfortable spot to be in, since you care about both of them. Do you know what the fight was about?
Kabir thinks Dev told everyone his secret. Dev says he didn't.
You don't know what really happened, so it's fair not to pick a side. You could tell each of them, "I care about you both, and I don't want to take sides."
Kabir got upset when I said that.
That is understandable, since he feels hurt. You can still be kind to him. Listen when he wants to talk about how he feels, without blaming Dev.
Should I try to get them to make up?
You could suggest it gently, but don't force it. Something like, "Would it help to talk to Dev directly?" leaves the choice with Kabir.
Okay. I just miss the three of us hanging out.
That's natural. Fights between friends often settle with time. Meanwhile, spend time with each of them separately, so neither friendship fades while they sort things out.
I'm hosting my first dinner party next Saturday. Six friends are coming.
How fun! Do you know what you want to cook?
I was thinking biryani, but I've never made it for so many people.
Biryani is a great party dish, but it's risky to try a new recipe on guests. Could you make a small test batch this week?
Yes, I'll try it on Wednesday. What should go with it?
Keep the sides simple: a cool raita, a fresh salad and something sweet like kheer or fruit. Most of these can be made in the morning, so you aren't stuck in the kitchen while your friends are there.
What should I pack for a day trek? It's my first time going with my office group.
Pack light. Carry two litres of water, some snacks like nuts and fruit, a light rain jacket, a cap and sunscreen. Wear shoes with a good grip, and take a small first-aid kit and a charged phone.
Should I wear jeans?
It's better not to. Jeans get heavy and stiff when they're wet or sweaty. Light trousers or track pants that let you move easily are much more comfortable for a long walk uphill.
I've got an interview for an internship on Thursday. It's online.
Congratulations! Online interviews need a little extra setup. Have you checked your internet, camera and microphone?
Not yet. I usually use my phone.
A laptop is better if you have one, since it stays steady. If you use your phone, prop it up at eye level. Test a call with a friend beforehand.
What should be behind me?
A plain wall or a tidy corner works best. Sit facing a window so the light falls on your face, not behind you. Keep the room quiet and tell your family the interview time.
What do I wear if they can only see the top half?
Dress as you would in person, at least neatly on top. Wearing proper clothes all over can also help you feel more serious and confident.
Our family wants to celebrate Lohri this year. We've never done it before.

Lohri is a winter festival celebrated mainly in Punjab in the middle of January. Families and neighbours gather around a bonfire in the evening, sing folk songs and share snacks. Do you have space for a small fire?
We have a small open area behind the house.
Then keep the fire small and away from anything that could catch, like dry leaves or cloth. Keep a bucket of water or sand nearby, and make sure an adult watches it the whole time.
What snacks are traditional?
People usually toss popcorn, peanuts and sesame sweets into the fire as offerings and share them too. Sweets made with sesame and jaggery, like gajak and rewri, are popular.
I'm the shortest player on our basketball team. Can I still be good?
Yes, absolutely. Shorter players are often quicker and better at handling the ball. Many teams rely on them to bring the ball up the court and pass well.
What should I practise most?
Work on dribbling with both hands, quick passes and shooting from outside. Speed and good decisions can matter as much as height. Practising these every day will help you stand out.
There's a full moon tonight. Why does it look so big when it rises?
That's called the moon illusion. The moon is about the same size near the horizon as high in the sky, but your brain compares it with trees and buildings nearby, so it looks bigger.
So it's a trick of the eye?
Yes, mostly a trick of the brain. If you take photos with the same zoom when it's low and when it's high, it will look about the same size in both.
Why does it look orange sometimes?
When the moon is low, its light passes through more air to reach you. The air scatters away more of the blue light, leaving more orange and red. It's the same reason sunsets look orange.
I'm going to watch it from the terrace with my brother.
That sounds lovely. Go out right when it rises, if you can, to see it at its biggest and most orange.
I keep starting books and never finishing them. Is that bad?
Not at all. It's fine to stop a book that isn't working for you. Reading should feel worthwhile, not like a chore.
But I don't finish even the ones I like.

Then it might be a time problem, not an interest problem. Try reading at one fixed moment each day, like on the bus or before bed, and keep the book where you can see it. Shorter books can also help you build the habit of finishing.
I got my board exam results today. I did worse than I expected.
I'm sorry. That's a hard feeling, especially after months of work. How are you holding up?
Not great. My parents haven't said much.
Silence can feel heavy. They may also be surprised and working out what to say. Would it help to talk to them about how you feel?
I'm scared they're disappointed.
They might be disappointed about the marks, but that's different from being disappointed in you. You could start with, "I'm upset about my results too. Can we talk about what to do next?"
What can I even do next?

There are usually options. Look at which courses accept your marks, ask your school about rechecking if you think there's an error, and talk to a teacher about your choices. One result doesn't decide your whole future.
I think I'll talk to my class teacher tomorrow.
That's a good step. Write down your questions tonight so you don't forget them. And be gentle with yourself this evening. You've had a tough day.
We found a tiny kitten crying near our gate. Its mother isn't around.

Watch from a distance for a few hours first, because mother cats often leave kittens while they look for food. If she doesn't return and the kitten seems weak or cold, call a local animal rescue group for advice.
Can I give it some milk?
It's better not to give cow's milk, as it can upset a kitten's stomach. Keep the kitten warm in a box with a soft cloth, and ask the rescue group or a vet what to feed it.
Grandpa plays chess every evening, and I'd like to learn so I can join him.
What a nice way to spend time with him. Do you know how the pieces move?
Only the pawns and the rook.
Then ask your grandfather to teach you one new piece each day. Play small games with just pawns and that piece. It's easier to remember a move when you use it straight away.
I'm worried I'll lose every game.
You probably will at first, and that's how everyone learns. Ask him to explain his moves after each game. Losing to a good player teaches you a lot.
Can I practise without him?
Yes. You can solve simple chess puzzles from a book or play against a friend. Then show your grandfather what you learned. He will probably enjoy that.
Our flat has a lot of mosquitoes in the evenings.
Mosquitoes breed in still water, so look for it around the house: plant trays, buckets, coolers and blocked drains. Empty or cover them every few days.
We have a water cooler on the balcony.
Coolers are a common breeding spot. Empty and dry it at least once a week, especially when you're not using it. Mesh on the windows and closing doors at dusk also help keep mosquitoes out.
It's snowing for the first time in our town in years!
How exciting! Snow makes everything look different. Are you going out to play?
Yes, my brother and I want to build a snowman.
Wet, sticky snow works best for that. Roll a small ball along the ground until it grows big enough for the body, then make two smaller balls for the middle and the head.
Our gloves are just cotton ones.
Cotton gloves get wet fast, and cold, wet hands hurt. You could wear two pairs, or put thin plastic bags over them. Come inside every so often to warm up and change into dry gloves.
My parents want me to learn classical music, but I prefer rock.
Both are worth learning, and classical training can actually help with rock. It builds strong basics like rhythm, scales and ear training. Have you told your parents how you feel?
Not really. I don't want to upset them.

You could suggest a middle path. For example, keep classical lessons for a set time each week while you also practise rock on your own. Showing them you're serious about music in both forms may help them listen.
My younger brother spends hours on games and gets angry when we stop him.
That's tough for the whole family. How old is he?
He's nine.
At that age, clear rules usually work better than sudden stops. Agree on a daily game time with him in advance, and give a ten-minute warning before it ends.
He still gets cross when time is up.
That's normal at first. Stay calm and keep the rule the same each day. Have something else ready, like a board game or going outside, so stopping doesn't feel like losing everything.
Should we take the games away completely?
That's for your parents to decide, but limits often work better than complete bans. Games can be fun and social. Steady rules, kept every day, usually reduce the arguments over time.
I'm thinking of changing my major from commerce to psychology.
That's a big decision, but many students change direction once they find what they enjoy. What draws you to psychology?
I took an elective and loved it. But I'm scared of starting over.
Talk to your college advisor about how many credits will carry over and how long the switch might take. Speaking to a few psychology students can also show you what to expect before you decide.
We're shopping for my little sister's school supplies and she wants everything sparkly.
Sparkly things can make school feel exciting for young kids. How old is she?
Six. But sparkly stuff costs more.
You could let her pick one or two sparkly things, like a pencil box or a water bottle, and keep the rest plain. She gets her favourite items, and the list stays within your budget.
She'll want the sparkly bag too.
Then let her choose: the bag or the pencil box. Giving a small child a choice between two things often stops arguments. She feels in charge, and you still set the limit.
Smart. I'll try it.
Make a short list before you go, too, so it's easier to stick to the plan in the shop.
An old man in our building lives alone. I'd like to help him somehow.
That's thoughtful. A friendly visit is a good start. You could knock, introduce yourself and ask if there's anything he needs, like help carrying groceries or setting up his phone.
What if he says no?
Respect that, and keep being friendly. Say hello when you see him and let him know he can call on you. Some people take time to accept help, and a regular hello can mean a lot.
We have a surprise quiz in English every Friday, and I always panic.
Surprise quizzes can feel scary. Is it the not knowing that makes you panic, or something in the quiz itself?
The grammar part. I mix up tenses.
Then spend ten minutes each day on just one tense. Write five sentences about your day in that tense. By the end of a week, you'll feel much surer of it.
What should I do when I panic during the quiz?
Take one slow breath and start with the questions you know. Easy answers first build your confidence. Then come back to the hard ones with the time left.
My uncle is visiting from Canada for the first time in ten years.
That's a long time! You must be excited. Do you remember him from last time?
Barely. I was five. Now I'm fifteen.
Then you'll be meeting him almost fresh. It can feel a bit awkward at first, but asking about his life there is a good way to start. What do you like doing?
I play the tabla and I like cricket.
Those are great topics. You could play something for him, or ask whether he follows any sport there. People who live abroad often enjoy hearing music from home.
He's bringing his kids too. They're younger than me.
Then you might become their guide. You could show them your favourite places nearby or teach them a simple game. Kids often bond quickly over play.
I hope they like it here.
With you showing them around, they probably will. Little things like local snacks, the neighbourhood park and family stories can make a visit memorable.
My friend copies my homework every day. I don't like it but I don't want to lose her.
It's fair to feel uneasy. Copying doesn't help her learn, and it could get you both in trouble. You can say no and still be a good friend.
How do I say it without sounding mean?
Try something like, "I don't want to share my answers anymore, but I'm happy to explain the questions to you." That way you're still helping her, just in a better way.
My grandmother's mango pickle recipe is only in her head. I'd love to write it down.
That's a lovely idea, as family recipes can disappear if nobody writes them down. Can you make it with her?
Yes, she's making a batch next week.
Then stand with her and note every step as she goes. Measure what she uses, even if she says "a handful." Use a cup or spoon to check how much a handful really is.
She never measures anything.
That's common with experienced cooks. Before she adds something, catch it in a spoon or bowl first, then write it down. You could also take photos of each stage.
Should I write down her tips too?
Yes, those are often the most valuable part. Tips like "dry the mangoes fully" or "use a clean, dry spoon" explain why the pickle turns out well. Add her little stories about the recipe too.
I'll make a small book for the family.
That would be a treasure. You could add other family recipes over time, with a photo of each cook next to their dish.
Our train is delayed by six hours. We're stuck at the station with two kids.
That's a long wait, especially with children. How old are they?
Four and seven.
Then find a comfortable corner, ideally in the waiting room. Get food and water early, before the stalls get crowded. Keep the kids busy with simple games like I Spy or counting trains.
The younger one is getting cranky.
He's probably tired. Lay out a shawl so he can nap on your lap, or take him for a slow walk along the platform, well away from the edge. A short change of scene often calms small children.
Should I reply to work emails on weekends? Everyone else seems to.
It depends on your workplace and your role. Some jobs need weekend replies, but many don't. Ask your manager what's expected, rather than guessing from what others do.
I don't want to look lazy.
Not replying on a Sunday isn't lazy if the email isn't urgent. Doing good work during the week matters far more. If something truly can't wait, people usually call.
Our society is holding garba nights for Navratri and I've never danced garba.
Garba is fun, and most of it is simple steps and claps. People move together in a big circle. Watching for a few rounds first helps you pick up the pattern.
What if I mess up the steps?
