Lots of people do, and nobody minds much. Start in the outer circle, where the pace is often slower. Follow the person in front of you and keep moving with the music.
What should I wear?
Traditional clothes like a chaniya choli or a kurta are common, but anything comfortable works. Wear light shoes, since you'll be dancing for a long time.
Do people play dandiya too?
Yes, often on the same nights. Dandiya uses pairs of decorated sticks that dancers tap with a partner's sticks. Hold them loosely and keep your eyes on your partner's sticks.
We lost our school kabaddi final by one point.
Losing by one point stings, especially in a final. How is the team feeling?
Really low. Some people are blaming our raider.
Blaming one player usually hurts the whole team. Every point across the match counted, not just the last raid. Reaching the final means the team did a lot right.
How can we bounce back?
Talk about the match as a team, calmly, and pick two things to work on. Then go back to practice with a clear plan. Remind each other that you reached the final together.
Frogs and toads look so alike. How do I tell them apart?

They are closely related, but there are a few common differences. Frogs usually have smooth, wet skin and long legs for jumping. Toads usually have dry, bumpy skin and shorter legs, so they often walk or make short hops.
Which one did I see near our pond with bumpy skin?
From that description, it was probably a toad. Toads are often found a little away from water, in gardens and damp corners. It's best not to touch them, and to wash your hands if you do.
My class is reading Alice in Wonderland. I find it really confusing.
Many readers find it confusing at first. The story works like a dream, so things change suddenly and don't always make sense. Which part confused you?
Alice keeps changing size and I can't keep track.

That's one of the strange parts. She grows and shrinks after eating or drinking things, like a bottle labelled "DRINK ME." You don't need to track every change. Just notice how each new size causes her a new problem.
Why does everyone in Wonderland talk in riddles?

Lewis Carroll loved word games and silly logic. The characters often take words too literally or twist their meaning, which makes the conversations funny and odd. It's meant to be playful, not a puzzle you must solve.
Who's the Cheshire Cat again?
The Cheshire Cat is a grinning cat who can appear and disappear, sometimes leaving only its grin behind. It gives Alice odd advice about which way to go.
Okay, I think I'll enjoy it more now.
That's the best way to read it. Treat it like a funny dream, and enjoy the strange characters as they come.
I feel nervous every time I have to make a phone call, even to order food.
That's more common than you might think. Many people prefer typing to talking on the phone. Planning what you'll say can help a lot.
What do you mean by planning?

Before you call, write down two or three short lines, like "Hello, I'd like to order for delivery," then your order and your address. Keep the paper in front of you. Small calls get easier the more you make them.
My hamster keeps running on his wheel all night and it squeaks.
Hamsters are most active at night, so that running is normal for him. The squeak comes from the wheel, not the hamster. Is his cage in your bedroom?
Yes, right next to my bed.
You could move the cage to a quieter room where it won't disturb your sleep, as long as that room isn't too hot, cold or draughty. Some wheels can also be tightened or swapped for a quieter one.
My mom said she'll buy a silent wheel.
That should help a lot. Silent wheels are made for exactly this. Your hamster gets his exercise, and you get your sleep.
Is twenty-four too old to start learning to dance?
Not at all. Many people start dancing in their twenties, thirties or later. Beginner classes are full of adults starting from zero.
What kind of dance is good for a beginner?

It depends on the music you like. Classes with simple, upbeat routines are fun for beginners, and salsa is good if you'd like a partner dance. Try one trial class of each and see which one makes you smile.
The power went out and our whole street is dark.
Power cuts can be unsettling, especially at night. Do you have a torch or an emergency light?
Just the torch on my phone. The battery is at forty percent.
Then save your phone battery. Use the phone light only when you need it, lower the screen brightness and close apps you aren't using.
We found some candles.
Good. Put them on a plate or in a holder, away from curtains and paper, and never leave them burning in an empty room. Keep them out of reach of small children.
How long do power cuts usually last?
It varies a lot, from minutes to many hours. You could ask a neighbour if they've heard anything, or check for updates from your electricity provider.
Why does it rain more in some parts of India than others?

Much of India's rain comes with the monsoon winds, which carry moisture from the sea. When these winds meet mountains like the Western Ghats, the air rises, cools and drops heavy rain on the side facing the sea.
So the other side of the mountains gets less?
Yes. By the time the air crosses the mountains, it has lost much of its moisture. That drier area behind the mountains is called a rain shadow.
I'm learning the tabla, and my teacher says my rhythm is off.
Keeping a steady rhythm is one of the hardest parts of tabla. Does it happen on fast pieces, or slow ones too?
Mostly when I speed up.
That's very common. Practise slowly until it feels easy, then increase the speed just a little. Speeding up only when you're steady builds control.
How do I know if I'm steady?
Practise along with a metronome, which gives a steady click. If you drift ahead of the click, slow down. Recording yourself and listening back also helps.
I'll try the metronome tomorrow.
Start with short sessions, like ten minutes, so you stay focused. Steady rhythm comes from daily practice more than from long sessions.
How can I make a strong password that I'll actually remember?

Try a passphrase: four or five random words strung together, like a short silly sentence, with a number or symbol added. Longer passwords are harder to guess, and a funny picture in your head makes them easier to remember.
Can I use the same one everywhere?

It's safer not to. If one site leaks your password, every account using it is at risk. A password manager can store different passwords for you. At the very least, give your email its own strong password.
My hostel food is terrible and I'm always hungry.
That's hard, especially with long days of classes. Is there a kitchen or pantry you can use?
There's a small common kitchen with a kettle and a fridge.
Then you can make quick, filling things: oats with hot water from the kettle, sandwiches, or curd with fruit from the fridge. Keep some bananas, roasted chana and peanuts in your room for snacks.
I don't have much money left this month.
Then focus on cheap, filling foods. Bananas, bread, peanuts and chana are usually affordable. You could also share groceries with your roommate to cut costs.
That's a good idea. My roommate likes cooking.
Then you two could plan a simple meal once or twice a week. It saves money and makes hostel life feel a bit more like home.
Is it better to buy fruit from the market or the supermarket?
Both can be good. Local markets often have fresher, seasonal fruit and let you pick each piece yourself. Supermarkets may be more convenient and have fixed prices.
How do I pick good mangoes at the market?
Smell near the stem: a ripe mango smells sweet. Press gently, and it should give a little without feeling mushy. Avoid fruit with dark soft patches or wrinkled skin.
Our neighbourhood park is full of litter after every weekend.
That's disappointing. Do you know if there are enough dustbins there?
There are only two, and they're always overflowing.

That could be a big part of the problem. You could write to your local ward office or residents' association asking for more bins and more frequent collection. A photo of the overflowing bins makes the request clearer.
Will anyone actually listen?
Sometimes it takes a few tries. Ask neighbours to sign the request too, since many voices carry more weight. Follow up after a week or two if nothing changes.
Maybe we can also put up signs.
That's a nice touch. Short, friendly signs like "Thank you for keeping our park clean" often work better than angry ones. Kids in the area could help paint them.
What's a good way to remember dates for history?
Link each date to a story, not just a number. Remember what happened, who was involved and why it mattered, then attach the year. A simple timeline on one page also helps you see the order of events.
I have so many to learn.
Group them by period, and learn one group each day. Test yourself by covering the dates and saying them aloud. Flashcards with the event on one side and the date on the other work well too.
My aunt keeps asking when I'm getting married. I'm only twenty-four.
That question can get tiring, especially at family events. How do you usually respond?
I just smile and change the subject, but she keeps asking.
You could give a calm, friendly answer that closes the topic, like, "I'm focusing on my work right now. I'll tell you when there's news!" Saying it with a smile keeps it light.
And if she pushes?
You can say kindly, "I know you care, but I'd rather not talk about it today." Then ask her something about herself. Most people move on once they get a clear, polite answer.
My friend group is planning a trip, but I can't afford it.
That's a tricky feeling, wanting to go but not being able to. Have you told them?
Not yet. I'm embarrassed.
Lots of people have money limits, so you're not alone. You could say honestly, "This trip is out of my budget right now, but I'd love to plan something smaller together."
What if they go without me?
They might, and it's okay to feel left out. You could ask them to share photos and stories, and plan a cheaper day out together afterwards, like a picnic or a film night at home.
A picnic sounds fun actually.
Then suggest it with a date and a place. Having a plan to look forward to makes missing the trip easier.
Why do onions make you cry when you cut them?
Cutting an onion breaks its cells and releases a gas. When the gas reaches your eyes, it irritates them, so your eyes make tears to wash it away.
Is there any way to stop it?
Chilling the onion in the fridge for a while before cutting can help, as the cold slows the gas down. A very sharp knife also helps, because it crushes fewer cells.
We're planning a road trip from Bengaluru to Coorg with friends.
That sounds fun. Coorg is known for its green hills and coffee estates. How many of you are going?
Five of us in one car.
Then plan a break every two hours or so, so the driver stays fresh. If more than one person can drive, take turns.
How should we split the costs?
Keep a shared list of fuel, tolls, food and the stay, with who paid what. At the end, add it up and divide by five. Agree on this before you leave, so there are no awkward moments later.
What should we see there?
Coorg has waterfalls, viewpoints and coffee estates, and some estates offer walks. Ask your homestay for local suggestions, since they know which places are worth the drive.
Should we book the stay in advance?
Yes, especially for weekends and holidays, when places fill up. Confirm the address and check-in time, and save the host's number in case you arrive late.
My new boss is very strict and I'm scared of making mistakes.
A strict boss can feel intimidating, especially at first. Do you know what she expects from you?
Not exactly. She gives short instructions and expects perfect work.
Try repeating instructions back briefly: "So you'd like the summary by four, under one page?" It shows care and avoids misunderstandings.
And if I still make a mistake?
Tell her early and explain how you'll fix it. Most strict managers mind hidden mistakes far more than honest ones. Over time, she'll learn she can trust you.
What is Raksha Bandhan about?

Raksha Bandhan celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters. A sister ties a thread called a rakhi on her brother's wrist, and he gives her a gift and promises to look out for her. Many families also celebrate it between cousins.
My brother lives abroad this year.
You could post him a rakhi with a handwritten card, timed to arrive before the day. Then set up a video call so you can see him put it on. Distance doesn't have to stop the tradition.
The inter-college table tennis match is in a month and I'm rusty.
A month is enough time to get back into form. When did you last play regularly?
About a year ago. My timing is off.
Timing comes back with practice. Start with simple rallies, focusing on hitting the ball cleanly rather than hard. Ten minutes of steady forehand rallies each session makes a difference.
What about serves?
Pick a few reliable serves and repeat them until they feel automatic. A short, low serve is a good one to start with. In a match, consistency matters more than tricks.
How often should I practise?
Aim for four or five sessions a week, even short ones. Play some practice matches in the last two weeks, so you get used to scoring and pressure.
Why do stars twinkle but planets don't?
Stars are so far away that they look like tiny points of light. As their light passes through moving air, it bends a little this way and that, which makes them twinkle.
And planets?
Planets are much closer, so they look like tiny discs instead of points. The air still bends their light, but the wobbles even out across the disc, so they shine more steadily.
So if a bright "star" isn't twinkling, it might be a planet?
Often, yes. That's a handy trick. A bright, steady light, especially in the west after sunset or in the east before sunrise, may well be Venus.
Can you suggest how to start a book club with my friends?
Start small, with four to six friends who enjoy reading. Pick a short book for the first meeting so everyone finishes it. Meet once a month at someone's home, and take turns choosing books.
How do we keep the talk going?

Ask the person who chose the book to bring three questions, like "Which character did you like least?" or "Would you have made the same choice?" Snacks help too. People talk more when they're relaxed.
Hi! I'm in class three and I have to make a poster about water. Can you help?
Yes, I can help. A poster about water can be bright and fun. Do you want to show how to save water, or where water comes from?
How to save water.
Good choice. You could draw three pictures: a closed tap while brushing teeth, a bucket instead of a hose for washing the car, and a leaking tap being fixed. Write a short line under each one.
What should the title be?
Try something short and catchy, like "Every Drop Counts" or "Save Water, Save Life." Write it in big letters at the top so people can see it from far away.
Can I use blue colour for everything?
Blue is perfect for water, but add a few other colours so the poster stands out. Green for plants and yellow for the sun would look nice with the blue.
Okay! I'll start after lunch.
That sounds like a plan. Draw lightly in pencil first, then colour it in. Have fun making it.
How do I get my dad to talk more? He only says "fine" when I ask about his day.

Try asking specific questions instead of "How was your day?" Something like "What was the funniest thing that happened at work?" or "Did you eat anything good at lunch?" gives him something easy to answer.
He's also not much of a talker in general.
Then doing something together may work better than sitting and talking. Many people open up while walking, cooking or fixing something side by side. The conversation often comes on its own.
Our friend circle has a group chat and I feel ignored there.
That can feel lonely, even with lots of messages flying around. What happens when you post something?
People reply to others but skip my messages.
Group chats move fast, and messages get lost easily, so it may not be personal. Still, it hurts. Do you feel included when you meet them in person?
Yes, in person it's fine.
That's a good sign. It may just be how the chat works, not how they feel about you. You could spend less energy on the group chat and more on meeting or messaging friends one to one.
Any ideas for using up leftover rice? We always cook too much.
Leftover rice is very useful. Lemon rice, curd rice and fried rice are all quick ways to use it. Which flavours do you like?
Fried rice sounds good. We have some vegetables.
Chop the vegetables small. Heat a little oil, fry some garlic and onion, add the vegetables, then the cold rice. Season with salt and pepper or a little soy sauce, and stir until everything is hot.
Why cold rice? Can't I use fresh?
Cold rice works better because it's drier, so the grains stay separate instead of turning mushy. Fresh rice is softer and tends to clump.
How long can I keep cooked rice?
Keep it covered in the fridge and use it within a day. Cool it quickly after cooking rather than leaving it out for hours.
My best friend lives in Kolkata and I'm visiting her for the first time. What's a must-try food there?

Kolkata is famous for its sweets, especially rosogolla and mishti doi, a sweet yogurt. Kathi rolls and puchkas from street stalls are also very popular. Your friend will probably know the best places.
She says she'll take me to a sweet shop on day one.
That's a great start. Try small pieces of several sweets instead of a lot of one, so you can taste more. Ask her which one she grew up eating.
Tomorrow I start a part-time job at a bakery. It's my first job ever, and I'm eighteen.
Congratulations! A bakery is a nice first job. What will you be doing there?
Mostly working the counter and packing orders.
Then learning the names and prices of the items will help a lot. Ask if there's a list you can study. Customers like it when you can suggest something.
I'm a bit shy with customers.
That's common at first. A smile and a simple "Hello, what can I get you?" goes a long way. It gets easier after a few days, as the same questions come up again and again.
What if I give the wrong change?
Count the change back slowly, out loud if it helps. If you make a mistake, apologise and fix it. Everyone makes a few counting mistakes at first.
My shift starts at seven in the morning.
Then set two alarms and lay out your clothes the night before. Being on time in the first few weeks makes a strong impression at any job.
We're throwing a small Christmas party for the kids in our building.
That sounds lovely. How many children are coming, and how old are they?
About fifteen, between four and eleven.
With that age range, simple games work best, like musical chairs, pass the parcel and a treasure hunt with easy clues. Mix the ages in teams so the older ones can help the younger ones.
Someone suggested a Santa visit.
Kids usually love that. Ask a cheerful adult to dress up, and keep small gifts ready with each child's name on them. A visit of fifteen minutes is enough to make it special.
Do I need expensive shoes to start playing football?
No, you don't. For a beginner, any shoes that fit well, grip the ground and protect your toes will do. Many players start in simple sports shoes.
My coach said studs would help.
Studs do give a better grip on grass. A basic, affordable pair is fine for now. Make sure they fit snugly, and wear them around the house a few times before your first match.
A big spider made a web outside my window. It's kind of cool but kind of scary.
Spider webs can be beautiful up close, especially with dew on them in the morning. Is the spider inside or outside the glass?
Outside. It sits in the middle all day.
Then it's quite safe to watch. Many web-building spiders wait in the centre for insects to get caught. The web works like a sticky net.
How does it make the web?
Spiders make silk inside their bodies and pull it out through tiny parts called spinnerets. They usually start with a few strong threads as a frame, then spin a spiral in the middle.
Should I take it down?
If it isn't bothering anyone, you could leave it. Spiders catch flies and mosquitoes, which is helpful. Just don't touch the spider.
I'll call it Mr Legs.
That's a fun name. You could watch how the web changes over the next few days. Many spiders repair or rebuild their webs often.
What's the difference between a novel and a short story?
The main difference is length. A short story can usually be read in one sitting and focuses on one main event. A novel is much longer, with more characters, more events and room to develop them.
Is Sherlock Holmes a novel or short stories?
Both, actually. Arthur Conan Doyle wrote Sherlock Holmes novels as well as many short stories. The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes is a collection of twelve short stories.
Which would you start with?
The short stories are a good start. Each one is a complete mystery, so you can read one in an evening. "The Red-Headed League" is a fun one to begin with.
I'm moving away for college next month and I already feel homesick.
Feeling homesick before you even leave is very normal. It shows how much home means to you. For most students, it eases as the new place becomes familiar.
What can I do to make it easier?

Take a few small things from home, like a photo or your own pillow cover. Plan a regular call time with your family. In the first weeks, say yes to activities, even small ones, so you start building a new routine.
My teacher praised my essay in front of the class and I felt weirdly embarrassed.
That happens to a lot of people. Being singled out, even for something good, can make you feel shy. How did you react?
I just looked down and turned red.
That's a natural reaction. Next time, a simple "Thank you" with a small smile is enough. You don't need to say more.
Why does praise feel so uncomfortable?
Some people worry about seeming proud, or about everyone watching them. Praise is often easier to accept in private. With practice, it becomes less awkward.
I did feel proud though, inside.
That's good, and you earned it. Feeling proud of your work is healthy. You can enjoy that feeling even if you don't show it to everyone.
Lately I've been snapping at my family, and I feel bad about it.
It's good that you've noticed. Snapping often happens when we're tired, stressed or have a lot on our minds. Has anything been weighing on you?
Exams, and I'm not sleeping well.
That combination makes anyone short-tempered. Try to protect your sleep a little, even during exams, since a tired mind gets irritated faster. A short walk between study blocks can help too.
Should I apologise to them?
That would be kind. A simple "I'm sorry I've been grumpy. Exams are stressing me out" helps them understand. Families are usually quick to forgive when they know what's going on.
My best friend got into the college we both applied to. I didn't.
That's a painful mix: you're happy for her and hurt for yourself at the same time. Both feelings are real.
I don't want to be jealous.

Feeling jealous doesn't make you a bad friend. It's a normal reaction to a loss. You can congratulate her honestly and still take time to feel sad. Then look at your own options, because one rejection doesn't close every door.
Mom and Dad said I can have a pet if I take care of it. I'm ten.
That's exciting, and a big responsibility too. What kind of pet are you thinking of?
A rabbit!
Rabbits can make lovely pets. They need space to hop, fresh hay every day, some vegetables and clean water. Do you have a place where it can live and move around?
We have a small balcony.
A balcony can work if it's safe and shaded, since rabbits don't cope well with strong heat. Your parents would need to make sure the rabbit can't squeeze through the railings or jump off.
What do I do every day?
Every day, give fresh hay, water and a few greens, and clean up its droppings. Spend some time with it, gently, so it gets used to you. Once a week, help clean the whole area.
I'll make a chart so I don't forget.
That's a smart idea. Tick each job after you do it. Your parents will see how responsible you are.
Why does my dog tilt his head when I talk to him?
Nobody knows for sure, but there are a few ideas. Dogs may tilt their heads to hear better, to see your face more clearly, or because they're listening for words they know, like "walk" or "treat."
He does it most when I say "park."
That fits the idea nicely. He probably knows "park" means something fun. He may be listening closely to find out if a trip is coming.
Our parrot has started copying my mom's ringtone all day.
Parrots are great copycats, and they often copy sounds they hear a lot. A ringtone is short and catchy, which makes it easy to learn. Does it bother your family?
It's funny, but my mom keeps thinking her phone is ringing.
That's a classic parrot problem. She could change her ringtone for a while, so the parrot's version doesn't confuse her. You could also teach the parrot new words or whistles to keep it busy.
How do I teach it words?
Repeat one short word clearly, many times a day, in the same cheerful voice. Say it at the same moments, like "hello" when you walk in. Reward it with a small treat when it tries.
Should I get one goldfish or two?
Goldfish are social and often do better with company, so two is usually better than one. But they grow bigger than people expect and make a lot of mess, so they need a large tank with a filter.
I only have a small bowl.

A small bowl isn't a good home for goldfish. The water gets dirty fast and there's little space to swim. It's kinder to save up for a proper tank first, or ask at a fish shop which small fish suit a small tank.
Hey, do you know any easy origami for beginners?
A paper boat, a cup or a simple jumping frog are all good first pieces. A paper crane is a classic, but it has more steps, so try it after a few easy ones.
I made a boat already. What's next?
Try the jumping frog. It's more fun because it actually hops when you press its back. Use a square piece of paper, and press each fold firmly with your fingernail.
My folds aren't sharp.
Thin paper helps, and so does folding on a hard, flat table. Line up the corners exactly before you press the fold down. Neat folds at the start make the later steps easier.
I've started a journal but I never know what to write.
That's common. A blank page can feel too open. Would it help to have a few starting questions?
Yes, please.
Try these: What was the best part of today? What annoyed me? What am I looking forward to? Pick one each day and write a few lines.
What if nothing interesting happened?
Ordinary days are still worth writing about. Describe what you ate, a conversation you overheard or how the weather felt. Small details become surprisingly fun to read years later.
How long should each entry be?
As long as you like. Even three sentences count. Writing a little every day is better than writing pages once a month.
What hobby can I do with my grandmother? She can't walk much.
There are lots of sitting-down hobbies you could share. Card games, carrom, jigsaw puzzles, knitting or sorting old photos into albums are all good choices.
She loves old photos.
Then an album project could be perfect. Sit with her, sort the photos and ask her to tell the story behind each one. You could write a short note under each picture as she talks.
I'm teaching myself the ukulele from online videos.
The ukulele is a great choice for teaching yourself. It's small and has only four strings. How far have you got?
I know three chords: C, A minor and F.
That's a strong start. Those three chords appear in lots of simple songs. Practise switching between them slowly until the changes feel smooth.
Switching is the hard part. My fingers are slow.
That's normal. Try switching between just two chords for one minute, counting how many clean changes you make. Do it every day and you'll see the number go up.
When should I learn the next chord?
Once you can switch between your three chords without stopping, add G. With C, A minor, F and G, you can play a huge number of songs.
That's motivating!
It should be. Pick one easy song with those chords as your goal for the month. Playing a real song keeps practice fun.
How often should I change my bedsheets?
Many people change them once a week, or every two weeks at most. If the weather is hot or pets sleep on the bed, more often is better.
Every week sounds like a lot of washing.
Having two sets makes it easier. Put a clean set on while the other is in the wash. Washing them on the same day each week turns it into a habit you don't have to think about.
Our house always smells damp during the monsoon.
That's common in rainy months, when the air holds a lot of moisture. Do you notice it more in some rooms?
The bathroom and the cupboard in my room.

Bathrooms need air, so leave the door or window open after use, or run the exhaust fan. For the cupboard, keep the door open for a while each day, and don't put clothes away while they're still a little damp.
Some of my clothes smell musty now.
Wash them again and dry them fully, in sunlight if you can. Sunlight helps remove the smell. Leave a little space between clothes in the cupboard so air can move.
Is there anything to put inside the cupboard?
Some people use small moisture-absorbing packets, or a bowl of salt or charcoal, to pull some damp out of the air. Replace or dry them out from time to time.
I'm decorating my small room on a tight budget.
Small changes can make a big difference without costing much. What do you want the room to feel like?
Cosy, and less cluttered.
Start by clearing out things you don't use. Then add a few soft touches, like a string of warm lights, a new cushion cover or a plant. Too many items make a small room feel crowded.
My walls are plain white.
You could put up a few of your own drawings, postcards or photos. Arrange them in a neat group above your bed or desk. Removable tape keeps the walls safe.
What's the best way to clean a really dirty stove top?
Let it cool fully first. Soak a cloth in warm soapy water and leave it on the dirty parts for ten minutes to soften the grease. Then scrub with a sponge and wipe it dry.
Some spots are burnt on.
Make a paste with baking soda and a little water, spread it on the burnt spots and leave it for a while. Then scrub gently. Avoid sharp tools that might scratch the surface.
It's going to be foggy tomorrow morning and I cycle to school.
Fog makes it hard for drivers to see you, so being visible matters most. Do you have lights on your bicycle?
Just a bell and a reflector at the back.
Ask your parents about a front and back light before tomorrow if you can. Wear something bright or light-coloured, and ride slowly near the edge of the road.
What if it's really thick?
Then it's safer to walk, take the bus or get a lift that day. Leave a little earlier either way, so you don't have to rush.
Why do we get rainbows?

Rainbows appear when sunlight shines through raindrops. Each drop bends the light, splits it into colours and reflects it back towards you. That's why you see a rainbow with the sun behind you and rain in front.
Why is it always curved?
Each colour reaches your eye from drops at a certain angle. All those drops form a circle around the point opposite the sun. The ground usually hides the lower part, so we see an arc.
Can you ever see a full circle?
Yes, sometimes from a plane or a high mountain, where the ground doesn't block the lower part.
What's the order of the colours?
From the outside in: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. Some people remember it with the name "Roy G. Biv."
I'll try to make one with a hose this weekend.
Stand with the sun behind you and spray a fine mist in front of you. Move around a little until the colours appear.
How do people know what the weather will be tomorrow?

Weather experts collect information like temperature, wind, air pressure and cloud cover from weather stations, balloons and satellites. Computers then use this data to predict how the weather will change.
Why are forecasts sometimes wrong?
The air is always moving and changing, and small changes can grow into big differences. Forecasts for tomorrow are usually quite good, but those for next week are less certain.
Hailstones fell on our street today! Some were as big as marbles.
That must have been a surprise. Hail can be loud and exciting to watch. Was anyone outside when it started?
My brother was. He ran in really fast.
Good thing he did, because big hailstones can hurt. Indoors is the safest place during a hailstorm.
How does ice fall when it's not even winter?

Hail forms high up in tall storm clouds, where it's freezing even on a hot day. Strong winds push drops up and down inside the cloud, and they freeze into ice layer by layer. When they get too heavy, they fall.
Our car has some small dents now.
That happens with large hail. Your parents may want photos of the dents, so take a few now. Next time hail is forecast, parking under a roof can protect the car.
What does a music teacher mean by "practise with feeling"?
It means playing or singing so that the music expresses a mood, not just the right notes. You might play softer in gentle parts, louder in strong parts, and slow down slightly at the end of a phrase.
How do I practise that?
Pick a short piece you know well. Decide what mood it has, like happy, calm or sad, and try to show that mood as you play. Recording yourself helps you hear whether the feeling comes through.
I've been asked to sing at my cousin's wedding sangeet.
That's a lovely honour. Do you know what song you'll sing?
Not yet. I want something cheerful that everyone knows.
Pick a well-known, happy song that's comfortable for your voice, not too high or low. A song people can clap or sing along to keeps the energy up.
Should I sing alone or with others?
If you're nervous, invite a cousin or two to join you for the chorus. It shares the spotlight and makes it feel more like a celebration. You can still sing the verses alone.
How can I help my two-year-old daughter enjoy music?
Two is a lovely age to start. Music at that age is mostly about play. Does she like any songs already?
She dances whenever a nursery rhyme comes on.
That's a great sign. Sing with her often, clap along and dance together. Simple action songs, where she moves her hands or stamps her feet, are perfect at her age.
Should I buy her an instrument?
Simple, safe ones are nice, like a small drum, shakers or a xylophone made for toddlers. Avoid anything with tiny parts she could swallow. Pots and wooden spoons work too.
Should she start classes?
There's no rush. At two, playing music at home with you matters most. A relaxed parent-and-toddler music group can be fun if you'd like one, but formal lessons usually come later.
She'll love banging pots.
She probably will. It may get noisy, but she'll be learning rhythm while having fun.
What's the difference between a raga and a song?

A raga is a set of notes with rules for moving between them, used in Indian classical music. Musicians use it as a framework to create many pieces. A song is one particular piece with its own tune, and often words.
So two songs can be in the same raga?
Yes, many songs share a raga. They use the same set of notes and often a similar mood, but their tunes, words and rhythms are different.
My grandparents in the village want video calls. Could you help me set them up?
Yes. First, check the basics: do they have a smartphone and a steady internet connection?
They have a phone, but the network is weak inside the house.
Then find the spot with the best signal, often near a window or on the terrace. Mark it for them, and suggest they take calls there.
My grandfather keeps pressing the wrong buttons.
Keep only the calling app on the home screen and remove the clutter. Teach him one thing at a time, starting with how to answer a call. Once he's comfortable, show him how to make one.
Photos keep filling up my phone storage.
That's very common, since photos and videos take up a lot of space. Do you have lots of near-identical shots?
Yes, I take ten photos of everything.
Go through them and keep only the best one or two of each moment. It's quicker if you do it weekly instead of letting thousands pile up.
What about the ones I want to keep?
You can copy them to a computer or an external drive, or back them up to cloud storage. Once they're safely copied, you can delete them from your phone.
Videos are the worst.
Yes, videos take far more space than photos. Delete the shaky or long ones you won't watch again, and keep short clips of special moments.
I'll start with last year's photos tonight.
That's a good place to start. Clearing old photos also makes it easier to find the ones you love.
Is it safe to use free Wi-Fi at a cafe?
It can be fine for simple browsing, but be careful. Public Wi-Fi may not be secure, so others on the same network might see what you send. Avoid logging into bank or other important accounts on it.
What if I really need to check something?
Use your mobile data instead for anything private. If you must use the cafe network, check that the website address starts with https, and log out when you're done.
Coding interests me but I don't know where to begin. I'm sixteen.
Sixteen is a great age to start. Many beginners start with Python, because it's easy to read. Do you have a computer at home?
Yes, an old laptop.
That's enough for beginner coding. Start with free beginner lessons online, and write small programs, like a calculator or a quiz game.
How much time should I spend?
Thirty minutes to an hour, a few times a week, is a good start. Regular short practice works better than one long weekend session.
What if I get stuck?
Getting stuck is part of coding. Read the error message carefully, check your spelling and try one small change at a time. A short break often helps you spot the problem.
How do I make friends in college? Everyone already seems to have groups.
It often looks that way, but many people are still looking for friends in the first year. Join a club or two that matches your interests. Seeing the same faces each week makes friendships easier.
I'm not good at starting conversations.
Start with something you share right then: "Did you understand today's lecture?" or "Is this seat free?" Small, simple questions open the door. Then listen, and ask a follow-up question.
I have to give a presentation in front of my whole department next week.
That's a big audience, so it's normal to feel nervous. What's the presentation about?
My summer project on water quality in our local lake.
That's a strong topic, since it's about a real place people know. Keep your slides simple: one main idea per slide, with a chart or a photo where possible.
How many slides should I have?
It depends on your time limit. A common guide is about one slide per minute. How long do you have?
Ten minutes.
Then aim for about ten slides, including a title slide and a final slide for questions. Practise with a timer so you don't run over.
What if someone asks a question I can't answer?
It's fine to say, "That's a good point. I haven't looked into that yet, but I'll find out." An honest answer earns more respect than a guess.
Should I take a gap year before my master's?
It depends on what you'd do with the year. A gap year can be valuable if you work, travel or build skills. What are you thinking of doing?
I'd like to work for a year first.
That can help in many ways. Work experience can strengthen your application and help you choose the right course. Keep in touch with your professors so they can still write references.
My parents worry I won't go back to studying.
That's a fair worry. You could share a clear plan with them: when you'll apply, which courses you're looking at and how the job fits in. A plan on paper often helps parents feel calmer.
I missed two weeks of college because I was sick, and now I'm behind.
That's tough, but it's fixable. Are you feeling better now?
Yes, much better.
Glad to hear it. Start by asking a classmate for their notes, and check whether any assignments were set while you were away.
There's an assignment due on Monday.
Email the professor today, explain that you were ill, and ask if you can have a little more time. Many professors agree when you ask early and politely.
How do I catch up on the lectures?
List the topics you missed. Cover one or two each day, starting with the ones you need first for upcoming classes. Ask a professor or classmate when a topic doesn't make sense.
I'm buying a gift for my boss's farewell. The team gave me the money.
That's a nice responsibility. Do you know what your boss enjoys?
She loves gardening and tea.
Then a nice plant in a pot or a set of gardening tools would be thoughtful. A good tea set or a box of special teas would also suit her.
Should we add a card?
Yes, a card makes it personal. Pass it around so everyone can write a short message. Keep the receipt too, so you can show the team how the money was spent.
How do I return something I bought online that doesn't fit?
Check the seller's return policy first, usually shown on the order page. Most give a few days to request a return. Keep the item unused, with its tags on and in its original packaging.
They want me to pack it myself.
Use the original box or a sturdy bag, and seal it well. Put a note with the order number inside. Keep the return receipt or pickup confirmation until the refund arrives.
We're buying a new mattress, and the shop has so many kinds.
Mattress shopping can be confusing. What matters most to you: firmness, price or size?
I like a softer feel, but my husband prefers firm.
That's a common difference between couples. Many shops sell medium-firm mattresses that suit a wide range of people. Some also sell soft toppers you can add on one side.
Can we try them in the shop?
Yes, and you should. Lie on each one for a few minutes in your usual sleeping position, not just sit on the edge. Try them together too.
How do we know if it's good value?
Compare the same size across a few shops, and check the warranty and return period. A longer trial period gives you time to be sure at home.
We'll visit two more shops this weekend.
Good plan. Note down the names and prices of the ones you like, so they're easy to compare later.
Our school fair has a stall budget of one thousand rupees. We're planning to sell lemonade.
Lemonade is a great stall idea. It's cheap to make and popular on a warm day. Have you worked out what you'll need?
Lemons, sugar, water, cups and ice.
Good list. Don't forget a big jug, a ladle, a table cover and a bin for used cups. Keep some money aside for extra ice, since it melts fast.
How much should we charge per cup?

Work out the cost of one cup first: add up everything you spend and divide by the number of cups you expect to sell. Then set a price a little above that, and keep it simple, like twenty rupees, so giving change is easy.
What if we run out early?
Keep spare lemons and sugar handy, and make a fresh jug when the first one is half empty. Running out early is a good problem to have.
There's a stray dog in our lane that some people want to drive away.
It's good that you're thinking about the dog. Stray dogs are often scared rather than dangerous, but some people worry. Does the dog seem friendly?
Yes, it's gentle with kids.

Then you could contact a local animal welfare group. Many help with vaccination and sterilisation, which makes neighbours feel safer. Talking calmly with worried neighbours about this can help everyone feel better.
Our community centre needs weekend volunteers to teach kids to read. I signed up!
That's wonderful! What ages will you be working with?
Mostly six to nine.
At that age, short, colourful books with simple words work well. Keep sessions fun and active, with reading aloud, talking about pictures and simple word games.
Some of them barely know the alphabet.
Then start with letter sounds, one or two at a time. Use objects or pictures, like "b" for ball. Praise every small step, since confidence matters as much as skill.
How long should each session be?
For young children, thirty to forty-five minutes with a short break is plenty. Shorter, regular sessions keep them interested better than long ones.
Our residents' association meetings always turn into shouting matches.
That makes it hard to get anything done. Is there a set agenda for the meetings?
Not really. People just raise whatever they want.
A short written agenda, shared a few days before, can help a lot. Give each topic a time limit, and let one person act as chair to call on speakers.
People still interrupt each other.
You could agree on a simple rule: raise a hand to speak, and only one person talks at a time. Write key decisions down and read them out at the end, so everyone knows what was agreed.
Every monsoon our area floods because the drains get blocked.
That's a big problem for everyone. Do you know what usually blocks the drains?
Mostly plastic bags and rubbish.
Then part of the fix is stopping rubbish from reaching the drains. A campaign asking people not to throw plastic in the street can help, along with more dustbins.
Who cleans the drains, though?
Usually the local municipal body is responsible. You could ask them to clean the drains before the monsoon starts. A group request with photos is harder to ignore.
Can residents do anything themselves?
Residents can keep the area in front of their homes clear and report blocked drains quickly. Don't go into drains yourselves, since they can be dangerous.
I'll bring it up at our next meeting.
That's a good next step. Go with a short list of problem spots and photos, and suggest one or two clear actions the group can agree on.
